'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)| 1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|de|Zwölf Erdzweige|ja|十二支|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Twelve Earthly Branches|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao|de|Yao|ja|爻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao|qq=}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)| 1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|de|Zwölf Erdzweige|ja|十二支|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Twelve Earthly Branches|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao|de|Yao|ja|爻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao|qq=}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)| 1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|de|Zwölf Erdzweige|ja|十二支|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Twelve Earthly Branches|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao|de|Yao|ja|爻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao|qq=}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)| 1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|de|Zwölf Erdzweige|ja|十二支|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Twelve Earthly Branches|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao|de|Yao|ja|爻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao|qq=}} of the Eight Trigrams.

revision.text:
'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)| 1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|de|Zwölf Erdzweige|ja|十二支|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Twelve Earthly Branches|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao|de|Yao|ja|爻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao|qq=}} of the Eight Trigrams.

revision.text:
'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)| 1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|de|Zwölf Erdzweige|ja|十二支|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Twelve Earthly Branches|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao|de|Yao|ja|爻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao|qq=}} of the Eight Trigrams.

revision.text:
'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)| 1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|de|Zwölf Erdzweige|ja|十二支|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Twelve Earthly Branches|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao|de|Yao|ja|爻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao|qq=}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)| 1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|de|Zwölf Erdzweige|ja|十二支|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Twelve Earthly Branches|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao|de|Yao|ja|爻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao|qq=}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)| 1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|de|Zwölf Erdzweige|ja|十二支|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Twelve Earthly Branches|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao|de|Yao|ja|爻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao|qq=}} of the Eight Trigrams.

revision.text:
'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)| 1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|de|Zwölf Erdzweige|ja|十二支|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Twelve Earthly Branches|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao|de|Yao|ja|爻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao|qq=}} of the Eight Trigrams.

revision.text:
'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)| 1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|de|Zwölf Erdzweige|ja|十二支|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Twelve Earthly Branches|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao|de|Yao|ja|爻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao|qq=}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen (Bagua)|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen (Bagua)|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|de|Zwölf Erdzweige|ja|十二支|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Twelve Earthly Branches|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Twelve Earthly Branches|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao|de|Yao|ja|爻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao|qq=}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen (Bagua)|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen (Bagua)|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.

revision.text:
'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen (Bagua)|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen (Bagua)|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.

revision.text:
'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen (Bagua)|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen (Bagua)|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.

revision.text:
'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|de|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen (Bagua)|qq=}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|de|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|de|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen (Bagua)|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian|de|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|de|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.

revision.text:
'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}} in {{ill|I Ching|de|I Ging|ja|易|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/I Ching|qq=}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han Dynasty|de|Han-Dynastie|ja|漢代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Han Dynasty|qq=}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|de|Jing Fang|ja|京房|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jing Fang|qq=}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yufan|de|Yufan|ja|虞翻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yufan|qq=}} of {{ill|Wu (Three Kingdoms)|de|Wu (Drei Königreiche)|ja|呉 (三国)|lt=Wu|lt_ja=呉|lt_de|Wu|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu (Three Kingdoms)|qq=}}. In this system the {{ill|Ten Heavenly Stems|de|Zehn Himmelsstämme|ja|十干|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten Heavenly Stems|qq=}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Five Elements theory|de|Fünf-Elemente-Lehre|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|lt=Five Elements|lt_ja=五行|lt_de|Fünf Elemente|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Elements theory|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}} and {{ill|Directions|de|Himmelsrichtungen|ja|方位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directions|qq=}} were assigned to the {{ill|Eight Trigrams|de|Acht Trigramme|ja|八卦|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Trigrams|qq=}}.
