Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|en|Zhen|WD=Q8070693|lt=Zhen (震)}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)}}, {{ill|Xun (instrument)|en|Xun (instrument)|WD=Q839767|lt=Xun (巽)}}, {{ill|Gene|en|Gene|WD=Q7187|lt=Gen (艮)}}, and {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Earthly Branches|en|Earthly Branches|WD=Q1072961|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao people|en|Yao people|WD=Q370868|lt=Yao}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|WD=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems}} to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|WD=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams}} in {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han dynasty|en|Han dynasty|WD=Q7209|lt=Han Dynasty}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|en|Jing Fang|WD=Q715480|lt=Jing Fang}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|WD=Q218652|lt=Five Elements}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yu Fan|en|Yu Fan|WD=Q1077571|lt=Yufan}} of {{ill|Eastern Wu|en|Eastern Wu|WD=Q274488|lt=Wu}}. In this system the {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|WD=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|WD=Q218652|lt=Five Elements}} and {{ill|Cardinal direction|en|Cardinal direction|WD=Q23718|lt=Five directions}} were assigned to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|WD=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|en|Zhen|WD=Q8070693|lt=Zhen (震)}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)}}, {{ill|Xun (instrument)|en|Xun (instrument)|WD=Q839767|lt=Xun (巽)}}, {{ill|Gene|en|Gene|WD=Q7187|lt=Gen (艮)}}, and {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Earthly Branches|en|Earthly Branches|WD=Q1072961|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao people|en|Yao people|WD=Q370868|lt=Yao}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|WD=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems}} to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|WD=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams}} in {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han dynasty|en|Han dynasty|WD=Q7209|lt=Han Dynasty}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|en|Jing Fang|WD=Q715480|lt=Jing Fang}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|WD=Q218652|lt=Five Elements}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yu Fan|en|Yu Fan|WD=Q1077571|lt=Yufan}} of {{ill|Eastern Wu|en|Eastern Wu|WD=Q274488|lt=Wu}}. In this system the {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|WD=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|WD=Q218652|lt=Five Elements}} and {{ill|Cardinal direction|en|Cardinal direction|WD=Q23718|lt=Five directions}} were assigned to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|WD=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|en|Zhen|WD=Q8070693|lt=Zhen (震)}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)}}, {{ill|Xun (instrument)|en|Xun (instrument)|WD=Q839767|lt=Xun (巽)}}, {{ill|Gene|en|Gene|WD=Q7187|lt=Gen (艮)}}, and {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Earthly Branches|en|Earthly Branches|WD=Q1072961|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao people|en|Yao people|WD=Q370868|lt=Yao}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|WD=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems}} to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|WD=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams}} in {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han dynasty|en|Han dynasty|WD=Q7209|lt=Han Dynasty}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|en|Jing Fang|WD=Q715480|lt=Jing Fang}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|WD=Q218652|lt=Five Elements}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yu Fan|en|Yu Fan|WD=Q1077571|lt=Yufan}} of {{ill|Eastern Wu|en|Eastern Wu|WD=Q274488|lt=Wu}}. In this system the {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|WD=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|WD=Q218652|lt=Five Elements}} and {{ill|Cardinal direction|en|Cardinal direction|WD=Q23718|lt=Five directions}} were assigned to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|WD=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|en|Zhen|WD=Q8070693|lt=Zhen (震)}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|ltq=Qian (乾)}}, {{ill|Xun (instrument)|en|Xun (instrument)|WD=Q839767|lt=Xun (巽)}}, {{ill|Gene|en|Gene|WD=Q7187|lt=Gen (艮)}}, and {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|ltq=Qian (乾)}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Earthly Branches|en|Earthly Branches|WD=Q1072961|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao people|en|Yao people|WD=Q370868|lt=Yao}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|WD=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems}} to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|WD=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams}} in {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han dynasty|en|Han dynasty|WD=Q7209|lt=Han Dynasty}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|en|Jing Fang|WD=Q715480|lt=Jing Fang}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|WD=Q218652|lt=Five Elements}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yu Fan|en|Yu Fan|WD=Q1077571|lt=Yufan}} of {{ill|Eastern Wu|en|Eastern Wu|WD=Q274488|lt=Wu}}. In this system the {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|WD=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|WD=Q218652|lt=Five Elements}} and {{ill|Cardinal direction|en|Cardinal direction|WD=Q23718|lt=Five directions}} were assigned to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|WD=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|en|Zhen|WD=Q8070693|lt=Zhen (震)}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)}}, {{ill|Xun (instrument)|en|Xun (instrument)|WD=Q839767|lt=Xun (巽)}}, {{ill|Gene|en|Gene|WD=Q7187|lt=Gen (艮)}}, and {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Earthly Branches|en|Earthly Branches|WD=Q1072961|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao people|en|Yao people|WD=Q370868|lt=Yao}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|WD=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems|1=Heavenly Stems}} to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|WD=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams|1=Bagua}} in {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching|1=I Ching}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han dynasty|en|Han dynasty|WD=Q7209|lt=Han Dynasty|1=Han dynasty}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|en|Jing Fang|WD=Q715480|lt=Jing Fang|1=Jing Fang}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|WD=Q218652|lt=Five Elements|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yu Fan|en|Yu Fan|WD=Q1077571|lt=Yufan|1=Yu Fan}} of {{ill|Eastern Wu|en|Eastern Wu|WD=Q274488|lt=Wu|1=Eastern Wu}}. In this system the {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|WD=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems|1=Heavenly Stems}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|WD=Q218652|lt=Five Elements|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)}} and {{ill|Cardinal direction|en|Cardinal direction|WD=Q23718|lt=Five directions|1=Cardinal direction}} were assigned to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|WD=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams|1=Bagua}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|en|Zhen|WD=Q8070693|lt=Zhen (震)|1=Zhen}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)|1=Qian County}}, {{ill|Xun (instrument)|en|Xun (instrument)|WD=Q839767|lt=Xun (巽)|1=Xun (instrument)}}, {{ill|Gene|en|Gene|WD=Q7187|lt=Gen (艮)|1=Gene}}, and {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)|1=Kun}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)|1=Qian County}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)|1=Kun}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Earthly Branches|en|Earthly Branches|WD=Q1072961|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao people|en|Yao people|WD=Q370868|lt=Yao|1=Yao people (Asia)}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|WD=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems|1=Heavenly Stems}} to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|WD=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams|1=Bagua}} in {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching|1=I Ching}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han dynasty|en|Han dynasty|WD=Q7209|lt=Han Dynasty|1=Han dynasty}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|en|Jing Fang|WD=Q715480|lt=Jing Fang|1=Jing Fang}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|WD=Q218652|lt=Five Elements|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yu Fan|en|Yu Fan|WD=Q1077571|lt=Yufan|1=Yu Fan}} of {{ill|Eastern Wu|en|Eastern Wu|WD=Q274488|lt=Wu|1=Eastern Wu}}. In this system the {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|WD=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems|1=Heavenly Stems}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|WD=Q218652|lt=Five Elements|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)}} and {{ill|Cardinal direction|en|Cardinal direction|WD=Q23718|lt=Five directions|1=Cardinal direction}} were assigned to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|WD=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams|1=Bagua}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|en|Zhen|WD=Q8070693|lt=Zhen (震)|1=Zhen}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)|1=Qian County}}, {{ill|Xun (instrument)|en|Xun (instrument)|WD=Q839767|lt=Xun (巽)|1=Xun (instrument)}}, {{ill|Gene|en|Gene|WD=Q7187|lt=Gen (艮)|1=Gene}}, and {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)|1=Kun}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)|1=Qian County}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)|1=Kun}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Earthly Branches|en|Earthly Branches|WD=Q1072961|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao people|en|Yao people|WD=Q370868|lt=Yao|1=Yao people (Asia)}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|WD=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems|1=Heavenly Stems}} to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|WD=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams|1=Bagua}} in {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|WD=Q181937|lt=I Ching|1=I Ching}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han dynasty|en|Han dynasty|WD=Q7209|lt=Han Dynasty|1=Han dynasty}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|en|Jing Fang|WD=Q715480|lt=Jing Fang|1=Jing Fang}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|WD=Q218652|lt=Five Elements|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yu Fan|en|Yu Fan|WD=Q1077571|lt=Yufan|1=Yu Fan}} of {{ill|Eastern Wu|en|Eastern Wu|WD=Q274488|lt=Wu|1=Eastern Wu}}. In this system the {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|WD=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems|1=Heavenly Stems}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|WD=Q218652|lt=Five Elements|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)}} and {{ill|Cardinal direction|en|Cardinal direction|WD=Q23718|lt=Five directions|1=Cardinal direction}} were assigned to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|WD=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams|1=Bagua}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|en|Zhen|WD=Q8070693|lt=Zhen (震)|1=Zhen}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)|1=Qian County}}, {{ill|Xun (instrument)|en|Xun (instrument)|WD=Q839767|lt=Xun (巽)|1=Xun (instrument)}}, {{ill|Gene|en|Gene|WD=Q7187|lt=Gen (艮)|1=Gene}}, and {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)|1=Kun}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|WD=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)|1=Qian County}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|WD=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)|1=Kun}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Earthly Branches|en|Earthly Branches|WD=Q1072961|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao people|en|Yao people|WD=Q370868|lt=Yao|1=Yao people (Asia)}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|qid=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems|1=Heavenly Stems}} to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|qid=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams|1=Bagua}} in {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|qid=Q181937|lt=I Ching|1=I Ching}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han dynasty|en|Han dynasty|qid=Q7209|lt=Han Dynasty|1=Han dynasty}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|en|Jing Fang|qid=Q715480|lt=Jing Fang|1=Jing Fang}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qid=Q218652|lt=Five Elements|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yu Fan|en|Yu Fan|qid=Q1077571|lt=Yufan|1=Yu Fan}} of {{ill|Eastern Wu|en|Eastern Wu|qid=Q274488|lt=Wu|1=Eastern Wu}}. In this system the {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|qid=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems|1=Heavenly Stems}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qid=Q218652|lt=Five Elements|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)}} and {{ill|Cardinal direction|en|Cardinal direction|qid=Q23718|lt=Five directions|1=Cardinal direction}} were assigned to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|qid=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams|1=Bagua}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|en|Zhen|qid=Q8070693|lt=Zhen (震)|1=Zhen}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|qid=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)|1=Qian County}}, {{ill|Xun (instrument)|en|Xun (instrument)|qid=Q839767|lt=Xun (巽)|1=Xun (instrument)}}, {{ill|Gene|en|Gene|qid=Q7187|lt=Gen (艮)|1=Gene}}, and {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|qid=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)|1=Kun}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|qid=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)|1=Qian County}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|qid=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)|1=Kun}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Earthly Branches|en|Earthly Branches|qid=Q1072961|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao people|en|Yao people|qid=Q370868|lt=Yao|1=Yao people (Asia)}} of the Eight Trigrams.

'''Nakkou''' (納甲) refers to the allocation of {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|qid=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems|1=Heavenly Stems}} to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|qid=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams|1=Bagua}} in {{ill|I Ching|en|I Ching|qid=Q181937|lt=I Ching|1=I Ching}}.
== Ten Heavenly Stems == The origin of Nakkou can be traced back to the method of xiangshu in the {{ill|Han dynasty|en|Han dynasty|qid=Q7209|lt=Han Dynasty|1=Han dynasty}}, which interpreted the forms of the trigrams as expressions of the natural order of heaven and earth. It is said that {{ill|Jing Fang|en|Jing Fang|qid=Q715480|lt=Jing Fang|1=Jing Fang}} perfected Nakkou by incorporating the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qid=Q218652|lt=Five Elements|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)}} into the interpretation of the trigram images, and that it was subsequently transmitted by figures such as {{ill|Yu Fan|en|Yu Fan|qid=Q1077571|lt=Yufan|1=Yu Fan}} of {{ill|Eastern Wu|en|Eastern Wu|qid=Q274488|lt=Wu|1=Eastern Wu}}. In this system the {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|qid=Q1190985|lt=Ten Heavenly Stems|1=Heavenly Stems}} and the concepts of the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qid=Q218652|lt=Five Elements|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)}} and {{ill|Cardinal direction|en|Cardinal direction|qid=Q23718|lt=Five directions|1=Cardinal direction}} were assigned to the {{ill|Bagua|en|Bagua|qid=Q340846|lt=Eight Trigrams|1=Bagua}}.

Here the trigram {{ill|Zhen|en|Zhen|qid=Q8070693|lt=Zhen (震)|1=Zhen}} is regarded as representing the emergence of yang, being assigned to the initial crescent of the month; subsequently, the moon was seen as evolving through the phases represented by {{ill|Dui|de|Dui|ja|兌|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|qid=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)|1=Qian County}}, {{ill|Xun (instrument)|en|Xun (instrument)|qid=Q839767|lt=Xun (巽)|1=Xun (instrument)}}, {{ill|Gene|en|Gene|qid=Q7187|lt=Gen (艮)|1=Gene}}, and {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|qid=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)|1=Kun}}. In this context the bright full moon represented by {{ill|Qian County|en|Qian County|qid=Q1201675|lt=Qian (乾)|1=Qian County}} was associated with Jia, while the dark phase represented by {{ill|Kun|en|Kun|qid=Q176459|lt=Kun (坤)|1=Kun}} was associated with Yi; the sun and moon were thought to meet as Ren and Gui from the north, before further entering the central positions of Wu and Ji.
== Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches == Subsequently, the {{ill|Earthly Branches|en|Earthly Branches|qid=Q1072961|lt=Twelve Earthly Branches|1=Earthly Branches}} were also employed, and the stems and branches were assigned to each {{ill|Yao people|en|Yao people|qid=Q370868|lt=Yao|1=Yao people (Asia)}} of the Eight Trigrams.
